exposure: Standardized Clinical Assessment and Management Plan (SCAMP) implementation
cohort: A total of 414 neonates with prenatally diagnosed congenital heart disease (CHD) from five University of California medical centers were included.
finding: Implementation of a Standardized Clinical Assessment and Management Plan (SCAMP) was associated with improved neonatal survival, increased birth weight, and reduced hospitalization duration in pregnancies complicated by congenital heart disease.
mod_finding: Survival following cesarean birth was significantly improved after SCAMP implementation, while no significant differences were found for induction of labor or spontaneous vaginal births.
